claims: Trump Accounts are tax-deferred custodial investment accounts for children under 18 with Social Security numbers.
Trump Accounts were launched via the "One Big Beautiful Bill" Act.
Trump Accounts allow up to $5,000 in annual post-tax contributions starting July 2026.
Trump Accounts feature a $1,000 federal pilot contribution for children born between 2025 and 2028.
Eligibility for Trump Accounts is U.S. citizen children under 18 at year-end.
Children born Jan. 1, 2025, to Dec. 31, 2028, receive a $1,000 contribution from the federal government.
Up to $5,000 annually post-tax can be added to Trump Accounts, including contributions from employers, families, or organizations.
Trump Accounts are managed by adults as custodial accounts until the child turns 18.
Earnings in Trump Accounts grow tax-deferred.
Parents use IRS Form 4547 to enroll in Trump Accounts.
A specialized portal is planned for Trump Accounts.
The $1,000 contribution does not count toward the $5,000 annual limit for Trump Accounts.
Funds in Trump Accounts are invested in index funds.
